builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL
summary: Replaces token-level supervised fine-tuning of open-weight LLMs for text-to-SQL with a constraint-aware set-contrastive objective at syntactic, semantic, and logical levels, supervised by LLM agents and verified by SQL parsing and execution on counterexample databases. Cost is a substantially more complex training pipeline (agent-proposed supervision, parser verification, counterexample database construction) plus reliance on the accompanying refined dataset, while single-pass inference remains cheap and fits one 24 GB GPU at the demonstrated 1.7B scale. It can fail when the verifier or counterexample databases do not capture schema-specific constraints, when agent-proposed supervision is noisy, and on databases or dialects far from the Spider/BIRD training distribution.
rationale: The accuracy and robustness gains over standard fine-tuning are large and the inference path is cheap, but adoption requires replicating a nontrivial multi-stage training pipeline that the reader should validate on their own schemas before committing.

claims.statement: Replaces token-level supervised fine-tuning of open-weight LLMs for text-to-SQL with a constraint-aware set-contrastive objective at syntactic, semantic, and logical levels, supervised by LLM agents and verified by SQL parsing and execution on counterexample databases. Cost is a substantially more complex training pipeline (agent-proposed supervision, parser verification, counterexample database construction) plus reliance on the accompanying refined dataset, while single-pass inference remains cheap and fits one 24 GB GPU at the demonstrated 1.7B scale. It can fail when the verifier or counterexample databases do not capture schema-specific constraints, when agent-proposed supervision is noisy, and on databases or dialects far from the Spider/BIRD training distribution.
Qwen3-1.7B execution accuracy rises from 62.9% zero-shot to 88.7% on Spider dev (89.2% test) and 73.4% on BIRD dev; inference is 0.42s per query, 23x faster than a GPT-4-based agent baseline.
